title: Your ballot. Your questions.
regional_note: Shared demonstration; label the example county and actual coverage.
scene_brief: One voter opens an official sample ballot, asks a plain-language question and sees covered KYV information plus the complete-ballot link.
ranking_reason: Clear product benefit; less distinctive as a story than the leading executions.

title: Show me the source.
regional_note: Shared source-checking lesson; verify the displayed source.
scene_brief: Jo opens the original source behind one candidate quote, then distinguishes attribution from proof.
ranking_reason: Strong source-access demonstration; 32 makes the same learning task more memorable as a skit.

title: Translate the amendment.
regional_note: Statewide measure only; local questions require different content and referral.
scene_brief: A single state measure is explained through current rule, proposed change and readable sources without a voting recommendation.
ranking_reason: Useful research question and clear visuals; needs current published state text.

title: Who sets the school calendar?
regional_note: General Florida board role; actual district dates or budgets would require localization.
scene_brief: A school-calendar question opens into one sourced school-board responsibility; a separate funding example can support the office explanation.
ranking_reason: Useful school-office companion; the GRWM execution in 31 has a stronger character setup.

title: Give election dates a place.
regional_note: Actual calendar dates and daily hours must match the county.
scene_brief: Mel adds current verified election information to a calendar already crowded with ordinary appointments.
ranking_reason: Concrete action; less distinct as entertainment and sensitive to the displayed county schedule.

title: Commute Update: Still Here
preferred_format: Commuter creator vlog with one sourced role reveal
regional_note: Different transit systems, roads, boards and funding records need separate local explanations.
scene_brief: Ray films a commute update without having moved; Jo follows one local transit or roadwork question to the operator, infrastructure owner and funding body.
ranking_reason: Repeated transportation situations plus a clear field-content premise.

title: There's more below the headline.
regional_note: Show only covered published contests, with the example county identified.
scene_brief: Scroll past a headline into one selected local contest and a useful sourced office explanation.
ranking_reason: Useful discovery but overlaps the clearer core demonstration and office stories.

title: Your county. Your voting details.
regional_note: A tutorial giving actual dates, hours or locations must match its county.
scene_brief: A short tutorial checks the county heading, election date, voting method and original official source.
ranking_reason: Practical and well supported; 34 supplies the stronger standalone story version.

title: One tax bill. Different jobs.
regional_note: Common role explanation; actual tax rates or local allocations require verified inserts.
scene_brief: A bill separates valuation, tax-rate decisions and collection; it does not imply one official controls all three.
ranking_reason: Useful household-cost companion; less distinctive than the power-bill story.

title: Before you forward it.
regional_note: Shared scene with one verified displayed source.
scene_brief: A hovering Forward finger pauses while a friend opens the original context and source.
ranking_reason: Compact source-check behavior; overlaps 32 and 34's stronger character reversals.

title: Make a plan before the day.
regional_note: Shared checking behavior; avoid presenting one character's county schedule as universal.
scene_brief: One person checks the official county page before choosing a voting method and making a plan.
ranking_reason: Clear practical need, with less comic story development than the shortlist.

title: Same county. Different ballot.
regional_note: Real districts and ballot examples require county-specific versions.
scene_brief: Two friends compare their real sample ballots and discover that districts explain different contests.
ranking_reason: Useful reveal, but depends on real ballot examples and careful district mapping.

title: First vote. Start with questions.
regional_note: Shared basics; date- or contest-specific answers require fresh official checks.
scene_brief: A person asks a basic voting question; Ray's overcomplicated explanation is interrupted by Jo's one clear answer.
ranking_reason: Direct learning demand and welcoming tone; just outside the shortlist because other scenes have sharper visual payoffs.

title: Who checks the gas pump?
regional_note: State inspection role; do not suggest the office sets fuel prices.
scene_brief: Dev asks who checks gas-pump measurement while Ray offers his cardboard Transportation Person badge.
ranking_reason: Memorable office connection, with thinner direct evidence for measurement-specific demand.

title: What they say-with the source.
regional_note: Shared demonstration of sourcing; verify the particular statement.
scene_brief: A candidate statement, original source and a visible note show what attribution establishes and what requires further verification.
ranking_reason: Important corrective companion; a complete-record promise exceeds current product content.

title: Requesting and returning are different.
regional_note: Statewide domestic rules; refer exceptions and individual questions to official guidance.
scene_brief: Two labeled checkpoints make requesting a mailed ballot visibly different from returning a voted ballot.
ranking_reason: Strong practical distinction, though less character-led than the top scenes.

title: Apartment Tour: Everything Costs Extra
regional_note: Shared fictional rental-search story; regional flavor optional. Specific land-use decisions belong in 18 or 23.
scene_brief: Ray tours an apartment he is still considering; Dev sells the parking-lot view as a premium amenity; Jo opens a housing/development question and the planning record.
ranking_reason: Closes the largest subject gap with an everyday moving-vlog story.

title: City? County? Authority?
regional_note: Use one verified site, jurisdiction and authority chain per local version.
scene_brief: A growth question moves from a building to a street to a map; Jo distinguishes the property owner from the responsible city, county or authority.
ranking_reason: Strong role-awareness need; more explanation-heavy than the leading standalone scenes.

title: Put the comparison on one screen.
regional_note: Shared product demonstration; label county, scope and example contest.
scene_brief: One actual covered candidate comparison opens its source links on the same screen.
ranking_reason: Strong product proof; works as a useful companion rather than the most distinctive social story.

title: When you need your voting details.
regional_note: Current official page and any displayed instructions must match the county.
scene_brief: An old screenshot fails to answer a current question; a tutorial saves the correct official county page.
ranking_reason: Concrete need improves the earlier bookmark-only idea; 34 delivers a stronger reversal.

title: Which information is here-and where's the rest?
regional_note: Shared coverage demonstration with explicit official referrals.
scene_brief: A real guide demonstration shows the useful covered information and the official resource for the rest of the ballot.
ranking_reason: Necessary scope honesty; overlaps 01 and works better as a supporting task than a leading story.

title: The election ends. Local decisions continue.
regional_note: Hold until after Election Day; any actual ongoing local decision must be correctly localized.
scene_brief: Ray rolls end credits after Election Day, but a public decision and Mel's next-month calendar bring him back.
ranking_reason: Keep for post-election continuation once updated evergreen content exists.

title: Budget Unboxing: This Decision Has a Paper Trail

title: When this street floods, who handles it?
